analysis:
Examined all units. The PR replaces Foundation Date `>=`/`<=` with `timeIntervalSince(_:)` comparisons to avoid a back-deployed weak-symbol crash on pre-release macOS 27.2, and adds a source-only lint script (scripts/check-date-comparisons.py).

ClusterPairCommands.swift (lines 119, 276): the deadline checks are `Date() >= deadline` rewritten as `Date().timeIntervalSince(deadline) >= 0`. This is semantically identical. It touches only CLI wait and teardown loop termination, with no auth, attestation, crypto, or key-handling logic.

DesktopAccountEarnings.swift (lines 67, 69, 75, 82, 102, 113, 115): the same mechanical rewrite for the read-only earnings aggregation windows. Boundary semantics are preserved: inclusive `>=`/`<=` map to `timeIntervalSince >= 0`/`<= 0`, and the remaining `<` and `>` comparisons are unchanged. Date values are not NaN, so there is no behavioral difference. No money handling is altered, and lifetime figures still come from the summary. This does not affect A-009 or any provider asset.

check-date-comparisons.py: a new dev/CI-time static checker. It only reads Swift files under repository paths with `Path.read_text` and prints findings. It has no network access, no subprocess calls, no eval, and no writes. Its heuristics can miss comparisons, and the docstring says so and names the binary check as the complete guard. Regex-based parsing could hit pathological backtracking (a CI availability concern only), but the inputs are repository-controlled source. This adds no runtime attack surface to the provider.

No threat-model assets, trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012) or threats are affected. Remaining integration questions: whether CI actually runs the script, and whether other `>=`/`<=` Date uses elsewhere in shipped source were missed. Both are outside the supplied evidence and are not security regressions.
